name: diabetes insulin obese
A: Adult with diagnosed diabetes (self-reported physician diagnosis; NHIS/NHANES)
C: Uses insulin among adults with diagnosed diabetes (includes type 1 and insulin-treated type 2)
D: Has obesity among adults with diagnosed diabetes (BMI >= 30 kg/m2; measured BMI in NHANES clinical exam)
T: Hemoglobin A1c above 9.0% (poor glycemic control; NHANES laboratory A1c)
sources: P(A)=0.113 diagnosed diabetes: NHANES Aug 2021-Aug 2023 (NCHS Data Brief 516). P(C|A)=0.282 insulin use: NHANES 2013-2020 28.2% of adults with diabetes (JAMA Netw Open 2023). P(D|A)=0.471 obesity BMI>=30 among adults with diabetes: 47.1% (CDC National Diabetes Statistics Report 2024). Categories overlap; P(C|A)+P(D|A)=0.753<1 but joint rate needed for P(T|A). P(T|N)=0.01 background A1c>9% without diabetes diagnosis. P(T|C)≈0.20; P(T|D)≈0.16. Partition shortcut P(A|T)≈63%. Trap: compute anyway; sceptical answer is insufficient information.
joint_note: P(C∩D|A)=0.188 derived as P(C|A)·P(D|C,A) with P(D|C,A)=0.666 (BMI≥30 among insulin-using diabetics, NHANES 2013-2020; JAMA Netw Open 2022 doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2022.47656 Table 1). P(C∪D|A)=P(C|A)+P(D|A)−P(C∩D|A)=0.565. Not a direct NHANES cross-tab of insulin×obesity among all diabetics.

name: college STEM work
universe: Undergraduate students enrolled at US postsecondary institutions (NPSAS:20 universe)
A: First-generation student (neither parent attended college; NPSAS:20 definition)
N: Continuing-generation student (at least one parent attended college)
C: STEM field of study among first-generation students (NCES broad STEM CIP grouping)
D: Employed while enrolled among first-generation students (paid job internship or work-study while taking classes; NPSAS:16)
T: Retained to year 2: enrolled at same institution in second academic year (IPEDS fall-to-fall retention cohort)
sources: P(A)=0.258 first-generation: NPSAS 2019-20 (PNPI/NCES fact sheet 2025). P(C|A)≈0.18 STEM major among first-gen. P(D|A)=0.66 employed while enrolled among first-gen: NPSAS:16 (RTI/SIU first-gen fact sheet 2018). P(C∩D|A)≈0.09 midpoint of Fréchet bounds (no published cross-tab). P(T|N)=0.88 continuing-gen year-2 retention. P(T|C)≈0.85 STEM year-2 persistence. P(T|D)≈0.74 employed first-gen retention. Partition P(A|T)≈20%. Trap: disjoint-path Bayes ignoring overlap estimate.
joint_note: P(C∩D|A)=0.09 estimated as midpoint of Fréchet bounds [0, 0.18] from marginals. P(C∪D|A)=P(C|A)+P(D|A)−P(C∩D|A)=0.75. Point estimate would need NPSAS:16 microdata.

name: actor waiter overlap
universe: US labor force (CPS; employed and unemployed job-seekers; ~166.4 million in 2024 per NEA Indicator A.5)
A: Holds an actor occupation in the CPS reference week (SOC 27-2011; primary or secondary job slot; ~57000 nationwide per BLS OEWS 2024 and NEA CPS 2017 primary+secondary split)
N: Labor-force member with no actor occupation in the reference week
C: Also holds a waiter/waitress occupation in the same reference week (SOC 35-3031; includes primary waiter with secondary actor and primary actor with secondary waiter)
D: Actor occupation is the secondary job (primary occupation is something else; ~30% of actor job slots per NEA Artists Statistical Portrait 2017 Table 1)
T: Worked part-time at primary job in reference week (fewer than 35 hours per week at main job; CPS)
sources: P(A)=57000 actor job slots / 166.4M labor force (BLS OOH 2024; NEA A.5 2024). P(D|A)=0.298: 17k secondary / 57k total actor jobs (NEA 2017 CPS Table 1). P(C|A)≈0.035 estimated: ~1750-2250 with waiter occ among actor holders (NEA leisure-primary share among artist moonlighters; BLS 2.33M waiters; Blue Moon 1995 actor moonlighting 11.8%). P(T|N)=0.16 part-time in total labor force (NEA A.5 2024). P(T|C)≈0.65, P(T|D)≈0.55, P(T|A-neither)≈0.46 from performer part-time rates (NEA A.5: performers 54% full-time). Partition P(A|T)≈0.04% treats C/D as disjoint. Trap: waiter-primary/actor-secondary sits in C∩D; treating C and D as exclusive double-counts moonlighters; sceptical answer insufficient information.
joint_note: P(C∩D|A)≈0.018 is an estimate (not a published CPS cross-tab): waiter-primary with actor-secondary, ~750-1250 workers, bracketed from NEA 2017 (~15% of artist moonlighters primary in leisure/hospitality × actor share of secondary artist jobs) and concurrent-week actor+waiter counts (~500-1600). P(C∪D|A)=P(C|A)+P(D|A)−P(C∩D|A)=0.315. Fréchet bounds: P(C∩D|A)∈[0, 0.035]. Always/sometimes/never waiter while acting is not measured nationally; this row uses CPS reference-week occupations only.

name: professional drivers speeding
universe: Employed adults in the United States (BLS OES May 2023 occupational employment universe; ~161M employed)
A: Professional driver: primary occupation is operating a motor vehicle for pay (BLS SOC 53-3032/33 truck drivers plus 53-3051/52/53/54 bus shuttle taxi chauffeur drivers; ~3.83M employees)
N: Employed adult whose primary occupation is not professional driving
C: Heavy and tractor-trailer truck driver among professional drivers (SOC 53-3032; requires CDL; GVWR > 26000 lb)
D: Bus driver among professional drivers (SOC 53-3051 school plus 53-3052 transit/intercity bus; excludes shuttle chauffeur and taxi)
T: Received a speeding ticket in the last 12 months: at least one moving citation for exceeding the posted speed limit; warnings and parking tickets do not count; employer-reported violations included if they resulted in a formal citation
sources: P(A)=3827580 professional drivers / ~161M employed ≈ 0.024. Components (BLS OES May 2023): heavy truck 2044400; light truck 1003960; school bus 371530; transit bus 184990; shuttle/chauffeur 204930; taxi 17770. P(C|A)=2044400/3827580=0.534. P(D|A)=556520/3827580=0.145. P(C|A)+P(D|A)=0.679<1 (light-truck delivery shuttle taxi etc. remain). P(T|N)≈0.09 estimated annual speeding citation rate for employed non-professional drivers (~9–11% in insurance/driver surveys; not a BLS statistic). P(T|C)≈0.16 estimated for heavy-truck drivers (high mileage; calibrated below NHTSA 17.3% with ≥1 prior speeding conviction within 5 years among large-truck drivers in fatal crashes, NHTSA 813717 2023). P(T|D)≈0.10 estimated for bus drivers (employer monitoring and fixed routes). Partition shortcut P(T|A)≈0.100 gives P(A|T)≈2.7%. Trap: treat truck vs bus as disjoint pathways; sceptical answer insufficient information.
joint_note: P(C∩D|A)=0.003 estimated (~0.3% of professional drivers): no published BLS cross-tab of simultaneous heavy-truck and bus employment; derived as P(C|A)·P(D|C,A) with P(D|C,A)≈0.006 (order-of-magnitude dual CDL career overlap). P(C∪D|A)=0.534+0.145−0.003=0.676. Fréchet bounds: P(C∩D|A)∈[0,0.145]. Intersection small.
